  "title": "Functional Spatial Role Encoding for Document Spatial Language Grounding",
  "core_problem": "Spatial language in documents — references such as 'the table in the right column', 'the caption beneath Figure 3', 'the highlighted value in the header' — requires mapping natural-language spatial expressions to functionally-typed layout regions. Current VLMs either apply raster-scan positional encoding that captures pixel geometry but not functional roles (title, section-header, table, caption, footnote), or compress page structure into a single globally-aggregated layout token that cannot serve as a per-zone self-attention anchor. No existing approach provides M named, geometrically-anchored functional zone tokens that the model's causal self-attention can selectively weight when resolving document spatial language: resolving 'the table in the right column' requires attending more strongly to table-role tokens whose bbox x_center > 0.5, a signal unavailable from a single global layout summary or a role-free uniform grid.

Decoder-only VLMs process all tokens — including any zone-typed prefix tokens — via causal self-attention; LoRA fine-tuning can train selective attention toward role-matched zone representations, but only if such per-zone tokens exist in the context window. The scope of this spatial grounding failure is demonstrated by BBox-DocVQA (Nov 2025): even Qwen2.5-VL-72B achieves only 35.20% mean IoU on spatial localization tasks despite providing correct textual answers (up to 25.51pp accuracy gain when ground-truth regions are provided), confirming that current VLMs systematically decouple answer generation from spatial grounding.

A critical evaluation baseline note: published VLM scores on DocVQA diverge depending on the evaluation protocol. In pure visual (OCR-free) evaluation — where the model receives only the document image with no OCR text augmentation — Qwen3-VL-Instruct-8B scores 91.6% (measured by DocCogito, arXiv:2603.07494). Official vendor leaderboard scores (e.g., 96.1% for Qwen3-VL-8B from the Qwen3-VL technical report) reflect different evaluation conditions (optimized system prompts, possibly OCR-augmented input or higher resolution settings). This protocol gap is methodologically significant: a paper claiming FSRTs improve a 95.7% OCR-augmented baseline is making a categorically different (and much harder) claim than one claiming improvement over a 91.6% pure visual baseline. This paper commits to pure visual evaluation throughout, consistent with DocCogito's protocol, so that gains are measured in a setting free of OCR shortcutting. A further evaluation challenge: standard DocVQA v1 has insufficient headroom in pure visual evaluation to isolate spatial-specific gains; meaningful evaluation requires spatial-term-filtered subsets of larger benchmarks (DocVQA v1 spatial, InfographicVQA spatial) and the purpose-built DocVQA2026 val to achieve both spatial specificity and statistical power.",
  "opportunity": "DocVQA2026 (ICDAR 2026) explicitly established spatial understanding — on maps, engineering drawings, and layout-referential QA — as a recognized evaluation axis for document VLMs across 8 diverse document domains. Although its competition closed April 17, 2026, its validation split remains publicly accessible (RRC platform; HuggingFace: VLR-CVC/DocVQA-2026; official evaluation code: github.com/VLR-CVC/DocVQA2026) with full local ANLS evaluation requiring no blind RRC server access. Confirmed dataset scale: 25 val documents and 48 test documents (73 total), where each row is one document with multiple questions. Based on the HuggingFace dataset viewer structure (each row contains a `questions` dictionary with a list of question IDs and question texts), the total question count per document varies; at observed density of 1–4 questions per document, estimated total val questions is 25–100. At n=50, 95% CI ≈ ±14 pp — making DocVQA2026 val a purely qualitative signal. The actual count must be confirmed by loading val.parquet programmatically before submission. DocVQA2026 val is retained as a conceptual primary benchmark — purpose-built for the spatial reasoning capability FSRTs address, covering novel domains (comics, engineering drawings) unlikely in VLM pre-training — but is framed solely as a qualitative and directional signal. Statistical power is achieved entirely by co-primary benchmarks: the DocVQA v1 spatial-term subset (~700 questions) and InfographicVQA spatial-term subset (~550–700 of 2,801 confirmed val questions), together providing ~1,250–1,400 spatial questions with 95% CI ~±2.7 pp at n=1,300 — sufficient to detect effects ≥5 pp with confidence.

DocCogito (arXiv:2603.07494, March 2026) is the most recent layout-aware document VLM and the closest prior work: it compresses page structure into a single globally-aggregated [LAYOUT] token via learnable weighted patch aggregation. CONFIRMED backbone: DocCogito explicitly uses Qwen3-VL-Instruct-4B and Qwen3-VL-Instruct-8B. In DocCogito's pure visual (OCR-free) evaluation, Qwen3-VL-Instruct-8B scores 91.6% DocVQA; DocCogito-8B scores 93.2% — a gain of +1.6pp from a single global layout token. The proposed FSRT method uses the same backbone (Qwen3-VL-8B Instruct) in the same pure visual evaluation setting, enabling direct apples-to-apples comparison: FSRT's M per-zone named-role tokens should provide at least the +1.6pp DocCogito achieves from its single global token, with additional benefit on spatial-specific questions where per-zone role+geometry anchors are essential. Note: The 4.5pp discrepancy between DocCogito's measured 91.6% and the 96.1% in the Qwen3-VL technical report reflects evaluation protocol differences (vendor card evaluations likely use optimized prompting, higher resolution, or OCR-assisted conditions versus DocCogito's strict OCR-free protocol). The proposed method adopts DocCogito's pure visual protocol for all evaluations. LayTokenLLM (CVPR 2025) encodes per-segment geometry without semantic role labels and requires a novel NTLP pre-training objective inaccessible within a 72-hour training budget. A lightweight alternative — injecting per-zone functional-role tokens as prefix anchors via a DocLayNet-fine-tuned role detector and training with LoRA — fills this gap and is feasible within the budget.",
  "landscape": "Layout-aware VLMs for documents include: DocLLM (Jan 2024, ArXiv, disentangled spatial attention on OCR bounding boxes, no role semantics); LayTokenLLM (CVPR 2025, arXiv:2503.18434, per-segment geometric layout token with NTLP pre-training, geometry only, no functional role vocabulary, +2.2 pp on single-page document understanding — evaluated from a lower baseline than Qwen3-VL-8B, so not directly comparable); LayTextLLM (ACL Findings 2025, interleaved bounding-box tokens with text, achieves 77.4% ANLS on DocVQA — substantially lower baseline; ablation shows +2.8 pp from layout tokens); DocLayLLM (CVPR 2025, visual patch tokens + 2D positional tokens + CoT pre-training, efficient but role-agnostic); DAVE (ICLR 2026, specialized vision encoder via self-supervised + supervised pretraining, +10.5% over SigLIP on document benchmarks, no functional zone encoding); SmolDocling (ICCV 2025, compact end-to-end document conversion, no spatial language grounding); DocCogito (arXiv:2603.07494, March 2026, single globally-aggregated [LAYOUT] token via weighted patch scoring — one token per document, no per-zone spatial targets — paired with a Visual-Semantic Chain structured reasoning format; backbone: Qwen3-VL-Instruct-8B; pure visual evaluation: Qwen3-VL-Instruct-8B baseline 91.6%, DocCogito-8B 93.2% (+1.6pp), InfoVQA 78.6, ChartQA 82.5, WTQ 58.3; ablation: removing layout tower causes DocVQA −1.6, InfoVQA −1.6, ChartQA −2.6, WTQ −1.9, TextVQA −1.0; but the single [LAYOUT] token cannot be differentially attended to for zone-specific spatial reference resolution). For spatial language grounding: Sparkle (EMNLP 2025 Findings, 2D spatial direction/distance/localization on generic images, no document zone semantics); SpaRE (ACL 2025, arXiv:2504.20648, 455K-sample spatial reasoning training for VLMs, up to 49% improvement on spatial reasoning benchmarks — generic image-space relationships, no document-specific functional zone vocabulary); GCoT (March 2025, step-by-step coordinate grounding for visual cues, treats all positions as geometry not function); Marten (CVPR 2025, arXiv:2503.14140, cross-attention interaction between visual and language tokens for attention-map-based spatial grounding in documents, no functional role vocabulary — demonstrates attention-based mechanism is viable for document spatial alignment); DocVXQA (ICML 2025, visual heatmaps for document answer explanation, does not model spatial language grounding); GETok (Dec 2025, uniform grid tokens + offset tokens for localization, no functional role vocabulary — 'caption' and 'body text' in the same grid cell are indistinguishable); BBox-DocVQA (Nov 2025, bounding-box-grounded DocVQA annotations with 32K QA pairs across 3.6K documents, geometric localization without role classification — demonstrates that Qwen2.5-VL-72B achieves only 35.20% mean IoU on spatial grounding despite correct textual answers, confirming the spatial grounding failure this paper targets — provides large training resource for spatial grounding supervision); DocVAL (arXiv:2511.22521, Nov 2025, validated CoT distillation for spatially-grounded DocVQA releasing ~95K validator-verified spatial reasoning traces via Google Drive at github.com/ahmad-shirazi/DocVAL — confirmed released as cot_docvqa.json and cot_merged_all.json — available as training data augmentation). Important evaluation protocol note: published DocVQA scores across these methods are not directly comparable when different evaluation protocols are used. DocCogito's pure visual (OCR-free) evaluation measures Qwen3-VL-Instruct-8B at 91.6%, while vendor leaderboard scores for the same model reach 96.1% under optimized conditions. This paper explicitly uses pure visual evaluation throughout to ensure comparability with DocCogito. The specific gap — M per-zone named-role tokens serving as self-attention anchors for spatial language in documents — is not addressed by any of the above: DocCogito's single [LAYOUT] token is globally aggregated; GETok's grid tokens carry no role semantics; BBox-DocVQA annotates geometry without role classification; SpaRE addresses generic image spatial reasoning without document functional zones; LayTextLLM/LayTokenLLM encode geometry without functional role vocabulary.",
  "approach": "We propose Functional Spatial Role Tokens (FSRTs) — compact embeddings encoding both a discrete role category and normalized bounding coordinates — prepended as a per-zone prefix sequence into Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct. Backbone selection rationale: using the same model family as DocCogito (Qwen3-VL-8B Instruct) enables a clean, direct comparison — both methods start from identical weights (Qwen3-VL-Instruct-8B at 91.6% pure visual DocVQA) and the only variable is the type of layout augmentation (DocCogito's 1 global [LAYOUT] token vs. FSRTs' M per-zone named-role tokens). Evaluation protocol: all results use pure visual (OCR-free) input, consistent with DocCogito's evaluation setting. The 96.1% figure from the Qwen3-VL technical report reflects a different (optimized/OCR-augmented) evaluation protocol and is not used as a baseline or comparison target anywhere in this paper.

A role detector fine-tuned on DocLayNet maps its 11 annotation classes to a 7-category FSRT vocabulary via the following deterministic mapping: {title} ← [Title]; {section-header} ← [Section-header, Page-header]; {body} ← [Text, List-item, Formula]; {table} ← [Table]; {figure} ← [Picture]; {caption} ← [Caption]; {footnote} ← [Footnote, Page-footer]. This mapping covers all 11 DocLayNet classes with no ambiguous residuals. Column position (left vs. right body column) is encoded in the bbox x-coordinate rather than the role category — a body-FSRT with x_center > 0.5 and one with x_center < 0.5 are distinct self-attention targets that resolve 'right column' vs. 'left column' references respectively, without requiring a separate column-identity role. A two-layer MLP projector maps (role_one_hot, normalized_bbox) pairs into the VLM's embedding space, producing one FSRT per detected zone (typically M = 5–20 per page). The prefix sequence is prepended before the image tokens and question tokens; causal self-attention at any subsequent position can attend to all FSRT prefix tokens, and LoRA fine-tuning trains the model to selectively upweight FSRTs whose role and geometry match the spatial predicates expressed in the question.

Architectural note: Qwen3-VL-8B Instruct uses the same causal Transformer LLM decoder architecture as Qwen2.5-VL, with a Vision-Language Adapter that compresses visual patch features via cross-attention before feeding the causal decoder. FSRTs are inserted into the LLM decoder's input sequence as prefix tokens — they participate in causal self-attention, not encoder-decoder cross-attention. The correct framing throughout is 'per-zone self-attention anchor' or 'prefix-position zone token.'

Key differentiation vs. DocCogito: DocCogito aggregates ALL patch embeddings into ONE [LAYOUT] token — no zone-specific token exists to attend to; 'the value in the right column of the table' cannot be resolved by attending to a distinguishable grounding target. FSRTs provide M named, geometrically-anchored tokens that causal self-attention can differentially weight based on spatial language predicates.

Domain generalization risk and fallback: DocLayNet was annotated on business and scientific documents; DocVQA2026 includes comics and engineering drawings. After Stage 1, manually inspect detection outputs on ≥5 held-out DocVQA2026 val pages spanning comics and engineering drawings; if detection F1 < 0.6, fall back to a coarser 3-class vocabulary ({text-block, figure, table}).

**Training pipeline — four stages:**

Stage 0 — Pilot experiment (~5 A100-hours, executed first to generate preliminary results): Use a pre-trained DocLayNet detector (publicly available on HuggingFace, no fine-tuning required) to extract zones from 500 DocVQA training documents. Initialize FSRT embeddings as simple untrained linear projections of (role_one_hot, normalized_bbox) — no Stage 1 pre-training. Fine-tune Qwen3-VL-8B Instruct with LoRA (r=16) for 1 epoch on these 500 examples with FSRT prefix. Evaluate on: (a) DocVQA v1 val full set (pure visual, ANLS), (b) DocVQA v1 spatial-term subset (~700 questions), (c) all available DocVQA2026 val questions. Acceptance criterion: spatial subset ANLS gain ≥0.3pp AND full DocVQA v1 regression ≤1.0pp — if met, proceed to Stages 1+2 with confidence; if not met, diagnose role detector quality and FSRT initialization before committing the full compute budget. This stage provides the empirical anchor the paper currently lacks and is sufficient for preliminary results in a short-paper or findings submission.

Stage 1 — Projector pre-training on DocLayNet layout reconstruction (~20 A100-hours): The two-layer MLP projector is pre-trained with a combined reconstruction objective L_Stage1 = λ_bbox · MSE(ŷ_bbox, y_bbox) + λ_role · CE(ŷ_role, y_role), where ŷ_bbox is a linear prediction of the four normalized bbox coordinates from the FSRT embedding and ŷ_role is a linear prediction of the discrete role class (7-way softmax). λ_bbox = λ_role = 1.0 by default; these heads are discarded after Stage 1 and only the MLP projector weights are carried forward. The VLM backbone is frozen during Stage 1.

Stage 2 — LoRA adaptation (~50 A100-hours): LoRA (r=64, all attention projections) adaptation of Qwen3-VL-8B Instruct on DocVQA training split augmented with templated spatial-language references to functional zones, supplemented with spatially-grounded CoT traces from DocVAL (confirmed released: cot_docvqa.json 71.1 MB, cot_merged_all.json 100.3 MB at github.com/ahmad-shirazi/DocVAL; if download is unavailable at experiment time, Stage 2 falls back to templated spatial-language question generation over DocLayNet layout annotations alone). Total training cost: ~75 A100-hours (including Stage 0). Total experimental cost including ablations: approximately 195 A100-hours.

Mechanism validation — attention routing analysis: Extract and visualize causal self-attention weights from the final answer-token position back to all FSRT prefix positions on 5–10 held-out spatial questions per zone type. If FSRTs with the role and geometry matching the spatial predicate receive systematically higher mean attention weight than non-matching FSRTs on the same page, this constitutes evidence for the attention routing mechanism. Marten (CVPR 2025) demonstrates that attention-based spatial alignment mechanisms are viable in document VLMs, providing architectural precedent.

Expected gains — calibration argument (corrected and validated): All calibration numbers use pure visual (OCR-free) evaluation, consistent with DocCogito's protocol. DocCogito-8B achieves 93.2% DocVQA from a Qwen3-VL-Instruct-8B baseline of 91.6% — a gain of +1.6pp from a single global [LAYOUT] token (confirmed from Table 2 of arXiv:2603.07494). FSRT uses the same backbone (Qwen3-VL-8B Instruct) in the same pure visual setting. The directional prior: M per-zone named-role tokens should provide at least +1.6pp DocVQA (comparable to DocCogito's global token), with larger gains on spatial-specific subsets where per-zone grounding is essential (a body-FSRT with x_center > 0.5 provides the specific grounding target for 'right-column body text' that DocCogito's single [LAYOUT] cannot). No specific pp gain claim is made; the Stage 0 pilot will produce the first empirical calibration point before full training. On DocVQA v1 (pure visual baseline 91.6%), gain magnitude from FSRTs alone is expected to be modest (likely 1–4pp); the evaluation signal for FSRTs is concentrated on DocVQA2026 val (spatial-by-construction) and the spatial subsets of larger benchmarks.

Evaluation hierarchy — three co-primary benchmarks (all evaluated pure visual / OCR-free):

1. DocVQA2026 val (conceptual primary, spatial-by-construction): 25 documents; estimated 25–100 total questions (actual count to be confirmed by loading val.parquet before submission; at n=50, 95% CI ≈ ±14 pp — qualitative directional signal only, not a statistical benchmark); purpose-built to require spatial reasoning across 8 domains; evaluated locally with github.com/VLR-CVC/DocVQA2026 scripts; ANLS metric.

2. DocVQA v1 spatial subset (statistical co-primary): regex-filtered subset of DocVQA v1 validation split (~5,188 questions total) retaining questions containing spatial terms ('left', 'right', 'above', 'below', 'top', 'bottom', 'column', 'row', 'header', 'footer', 'first', 'last', 'beside', 'adjacent') → approximately 600–900 questions; 95% CI ~±3.5 pp at n=700.

3. InfographicVQA spatial subset (statistical co-primary): regex-filtered subset of InfographicVQA validation split (confirmed: 500 images, 2,801 questions); estimated ~550–700 spatial-term questions; 95% CI ~±3.5 pp at n=600.

The two larger benchmarks together yield approximately 1,250–1,400 spatial questions; joint evidence provides 95% CI ~±2.7 pp at n=1,300 — sufficient to detect effects ≥5 pp with statistical confidence. Primary metric: ANLS on DocVQA2026 val (qualitative directional signal) and spatial subsets (statistical backbone); secondary metric: spatial vs. non-spatial ANLS ratio demonstrating specificity of gains.",

  "description": "This paper addresses a critical gap in document Visual Question Answering: the inability of current VLMs to resolve spatial language expressions ('the table in the right column', 'the caption beneath Figure 3') to functionally-typed layout regions. BBox-DocVQA (Nov 2025) quantifies this gap: even Qwen2.5-VL-72B achieves only 35.20% mean IoU on spatial localization despite correct textual answers, with up to 25.51 pp accuracy gain when ground-truth regions are provided. Existing models either apply raster-scan positional encoding (geometry only, no role semantics) or compress page structure into a single globally-aggregated layout token (DocCogito) that cannot serve as a per-zone self-attention anchor.

We propose Functional Spatial Role Tokens (FSRTs) — per-zone embeddings encoding both a discrete role category and normalized bounding coordinates — prepended as a prefix sequence to Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct. Backbone selection: we use the same backbone as DocCogito (Qwen3-VL-Instruct-8B) to enable a direct apples-to-apples comparison. All evaluations use pure visual (OCR-free) input, consistent with DocCogito's evaluation protocol. Under this protocol, the Qwen3-VL-Instruct-8B baseline is 91.6% DocVQA (per DocCogito's measurement); DocCogito achieves 93.2% (+1.6pp) by adding a single global [LAYOUT] token. The proposed FSRT method targets >93.2% DocVQA plus larger gains on spatial-specific tasks, enabled by M per-zone named-role tokens that causal self-attention can differentially weight. Note: the commonly cited 96.1% Qwen3-VL-8B score reflects a different (optimized/OCR-augmented) evaluation protocol and is not used as a comparison target.

A DocLayNet-fine-tuned role detector produces zone detections using a 7-category vocabulary ({title, section-header, body, table, figure, caption, footnote}) mapped from DocLayNet's 11 classes via a deterministic rule. Column position is encoded in the bbox x-coordinate, so body-FSRTs with x_center > 0.5 vs. < 0.5 are distinct self-attention anchors enabling resolution of 'right column' references. A two-layer MLP projector maps (role_one_hot, normalized_bbox) into the VLM embedding space.

The paper targets **both** accuracy improvement and explainability. EaGERS aims to "enforce that the answer can be reconstructed solely from document regions that are explicitly grounded and verbalised" without model fine-tuning, addressing the problem of "lack of clear grounding between answers and source regions."

The authors use an ensemble of three pretrained models: "BLIP, CLIP, and ALIGN to generate embeddings in a complementary way in order to mitigate specific biases."

**Not addressed.** The paper uses a uniform fixed grid (5×5 or 5×10 cells) with cosine similarity ranking. The paper does not discuss prefix-token or prompt-based methods. Key architectural constraints mentioned include:
- Dependence on VLM-generated explanations that may be inaccurate
- Grid-based masking causing boundary artifacts (15% margin improvement suggests this issue)
- Higher computational cost (2.4× slower inference)
